Treat audio as always produced and the flag as a billing choice you cannot verify from the docs; leaving it false may still return a clip with sound. duration_seconds is INT min 4 max 8 step 2, which is exactly the documented 4, 6, 8. One video per request, 24 fps. Prompt limit is 1,024 tokens, not characters. person_generation is an extra: text to video accepts only 'allow_all' upstream, so sending 'BLOCK' may fail.

Omni Flash.label: Gemini Omni Flash

constraints.note: This model is running as text to video, so it takes no attached picture or clip.

price.note: Flat per second at 720p. Duration cannot be set as a parameter, so a request costs whatever length the model returns: 3 s is about 46 credits and 10 s about 306 credits from the same click.

Omni Flash.strengths: Native audio and multi-input reasoning, 720p only
Omni Flash.notes: DURATION IS NOT A PARAMETER. The length is written into the prompt ('a 6-second clip'); the model may return 3 to 10 seconds and defaults to 10. Because the price is per second, the estimate for this model is a range, not a number, and the picker should say so. On the older GeminiVideoOmni node the aspect ratio also has to be written into the prompt; GeminiVideoOmniV2 exposes aspect_ratio and task_type as real inputs, so prefer it. MISMATCH: both nodes expose temperature and top_p for this model and send them in generation_config, but Google's Omni limitations say 'System instructions, temperature, top_p, stop sequences, and negative prompts are not supported'. Superseded by Omni Flash 1.1.

Omni Flash 1.1.label: Gemini Omni Flash 1.1

constraints.note: This model is running as text to video, so it takes no attached picture or clip.

price.note: Per second. Because duration is prompt-controlled and defaults to 10 s, a single default click at 720p costs about $1.45 (306 credits) and at 4k about $4.35 (918 credits). Show a range and warn before the click.

Omni Flash 1.1.strengths: Google's default video model, 360p to 4k with native audio
Omni Flash 1.1.notes: Duration is prompt-controlled and defaults to 10 seconds, so this is the single most dangerous model in the catalog for an unexpected bill. 1080p and 4k are documented as upscaled, not native. task_type has six values; use 'text_to_video' for the picker's text to video path ('auto' also works with no media attached). Unlike the older Omni Flash, this model exposes no temperature or top_p, which matches Google's documented limitations.

OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2/gpt-image-2.5-flare.label: GPT Image 2.5 Flare

capabilities.outputSize: Eight pixel presets from 1024x1024 to 3840x2160, plus auto and a custom size

price.note: Exact per size and per quality, read out of the node's own price_badge table rather than typed: forty figures, so they come from the machine. GPT Image bills on tokens and the token count follows the size the model actually returns, so every figure here is a floor. Each one therefore carries a span from the preset up to the top of that quality's own published range (low runs to 5.97 credits, max to 214.69), which is what makes every surface say "about" rather than quote a preset as if it were a bill. A reference image adds 0.0117 to 0.0176 US dollars each on top, which estimateCredits does not model yet. The node's price badge bills every reference image, including the first, at 0.0117 to 0.0176 US dollars each (2.47 to 3.71 credits).

Quality runs low, medium, high, xhigh, max, two rungs above anything gpt-image-2 offers, and `background` offers auto, opaque and transparent, as gpt-image-2 does since the 2026-09-24 catalog. Up to 16 reference images through the same dotted group Seedream uses, and an optional mask.
